# v3.29

Rolls up the seven dev pre-releases since v3.22 — **v3.23-dev** through **v3.29-dev**.

The theme is the **training catalogue**, and specifically what happens to entries the system creates for itself. When a student import meets a training title it doesn't recognise it invents a catalogue entry, and this release fixes what the app then did with those entries: it presented values nobody had chosen as though they were chosen, counted them in your figures as though they were real, and gave you no way to say "this one isn't needed". Alongside that, two OLX display bugs and one import fault that was quietly losing data.

## Fixed — imported entries no longer pretend to be classified

A training entry created by an import knows only the training's *name*. Its **Type**, **Product** and **Function** have to hold something, so the import filled them in — always `Certification`, always `Sales`, and whichever product type happened to sort first. Those invented values were then shown as if an admin had picked them, so every row in the amber **"needs attention"** list looked reviewed and finished when nothing had been reviewed at all.

- Those three fields now read **Not set** until you choose them.
- **"Mark as Complete" has been replaced.** It performed no checks and was clickable without ever opening the entry, so one click promoted the invented values into your catalogue. Completing an entry now means opening it, choosing the three values, and pressing **Save & Complete** — which refuses to save while any of them is unset.
- A failed save in that list is now reported instead of looking identical to a success.

## Fixed — unreviewed entries no longer count in your figures

Those same entries were being counted everywhere — the dashboard, every report, scheduled exports and the public API — as genuine **Certifications** in the **Sales** function. Real completions filed under a category nobody picked, inflating certification counts and skewing the by-product and by-function breakdowns.

Unreviewed entries are now held back from all reporting until an admin classifies them, and appear everywhere the moment they do. **Catalogue Health** was worst affected and is corrected too.

Partner program compliance could also pick these entries up on its own: requirements count everyone holding any catalogue variant of the required training, matched on Full Title and type, and a freshly imported entry takes the imported title as its Full Title with `Certification` as its placeholder type. One whose name matched a required certification's Full Title would join that requirement and add its holders to the attained count — without anyone having configured it. They are now left out of that match, and out of the training picker used to set requirements up.

> **Expect your certification counts to fall** if you have entries waiting in the amber list. That is the correction, not a regression. SuperAdmins now see a notice on the dashboard saying how many entries are outstanding and that they are excluded, so the gap is visible rather than silent — and the numbers return as you classify them.

## New — ignore the entries you don't need

Some entries simply aren't wanted, and until now the only options were to fill one in properly or delete it, losing the record that people had completed it.

**Ignore** is available on each row of the **"needs attention"** list, and on the **Full Title** page where it applies to every training title at once. An ignored entry is left out of the dashboard, every report, exports and the public API, is no longer offered when setting up program or offering requirements, and carries a grey **Ignored** badge. **Restore** undoes it. Nothing is deleted — the completions are kept, so a learner's own record still shows the training.

A **Show ignored only** tickbox beside **Show legacy only** narrows the catalogue to ignored entries, and is remembered when you open one and click Back.

## New — see what an unreviewed entry is costing

The "needs attention" list has an **Excluded** column: how many learners have completed that training and are being held out of reporting until someone reviews it. It tells you at a glance which entries actually matter and which to simply ignore.

## Fixed — two OLX display faults

- **Sub-items attached to a parent were impossible to find.** Searching for one returned nothing, and filtering **Type** to *OLX Sub-Item* returned nothing either — that filter also removes the OLX parents, taking their nested rows with them. The only way to edit one was to detach it from its parent, edit it, and re-attach. Searching, or filtering to *OLX Sub-Item*, now brings matching sub-items up as ordinary rows, each labelled with its parent.
- **Expanding an OLX showed duplicates.** A parent records its sub-items by Training Title, and several of those often map to one Full Title, so each variant produced its own row — a parent with three sub-items reading "6 sub-items" and listing every name twice. Sub-items now collapse to one row per Full Title, with a count of how many Training Titles each covers.

## Fixed — importing a training file could wipe your Legacy settings

If the file you imported didn't happen to include a **Legacy** column, every row it touched had its legacy marker *and* its replacement list silently cleared. An import that looked like it was only updating the columns present was undoing work elsewhere, visible later only as a legacy cert that had stopped being flagged.

Legacy, Replacement and Ignored are now resolved against what is already stored: a column absent from your file leaves that value alone, and only a mapped column can change it. A blank cell in a mapped column still means "not legacy", and changing a training to a type that cannot be legacy still clears it.

> This fault has been present since the legacy feature shipped. The fix stops further loss but cannot recover what was already cleared — **worth reviewing your Legacy settings after upgrading**. The Legacy Replacement Gap report is the quickest way to spot certs that should be flagged and aren't.

## Behind the scenes

A note in the developer documentation about how help text is compiled was wrong in every particular, and had sent three separate reviews hunting for problems that did not exist. It has been corrected, and replaced with a check that runs on every build — so the class of bug it was meant to describe (two words rendering with no space between them) is now caught automatically rather than argued about.

## Upgrading

This release includes a **database migration** — a single new column with a default, applied automatically on update. As with any schema change, take a backup first.
